title: Contrast-Adaptive Inference for Propensity-Trimmed Causal Means with Continuous Doses
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier subfield below field floor; paper score ceiling 7.3 < 7.4 and not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: Its contribution is nevertheless confined to a highly structured benchmark with one scalar covariate, known C2 smoothness constants, uniform overlap, binary outcomes, and a monotone transverse single crossing, so it does not establish a general frontier for hard propensity trimming.
The motivating NMES use is not analyzed, and the construction's very conservative gates and constants leave its practical inferential value unsupported beyond the rate theorem.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched rate for estimation and both interval-honesty criteria, with one eta-free full-class-honest interval, and the D0.5 math panel passed without findings. The novelty gate capped the delivered scalar benchmark at subfield (score 7.3 below the field threshold 7.4); two decision-panel positioning and bibliography findings remain. A field re-raise needs broader theory or substantive practical analysis, not another prose-only cycle.
tldr: For the hard propensity-trimmed causal mean on the restricted scalar-covariate, binary-outcome, compact-support, uniformly overlapping, twice continuously differentiable, monotone single-crossing class \(\mathcal P\), estimation risk, subclass-honest expected length, and full-class-honest expected length all have frontier \(n^{-2/5}+\eta n^{-1/3}\). One fully observable estimator and one \(\eta\)-free interval attain every contrast-subclass rate simultaneously, while that interval remains honest over all of \(\mathcal P\). Thus contrast adaptation and strengthening coverage from \(\mathcal P_\eta\) to \(\mathcal P\) have no minimax-rate cost on this class. Class inclusion transfers only the lower bounds to broader hard-target models; neither the upper certificate nor the matching frontier is claimed beyond \(\mathcal P\).
gap: Published continuous-dose trimming theory obtains regular inference by fixing smoothing in the dose and trimming indicator. Generic level-set and upper-contour theory does not address a normalized conditional treatment density, a selected causal ratio, cancellation at zero boundary contrast, and interval length on nested subclasses under coverage over the full class.
fill: The project derives legal lower experiments and asks whether the explicit sample-split construction, whose nuisance queries are confined to \(D=[5/8,7/8]\), satisfies the rederived second- and fourth-moment envelopes, the three-event \(37/40\) coverage ledger, and the unconditional expected-length bound, yielding the sharp frontier and the transition \(\eta=n^{-1/15}\).
